answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Written in a cause and effect, two sentences register, it stays short. Reaching the dune of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. The umber holds work receipts rather than names, so the dawn of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. The design leans on invitation quota tree, revoked by a single upheld challenge, every claim is re-checked by someone with nothing to gain.
